Play

Finding your footing

5 min

When tools are unfamiliar (like Godot), just getting set up to work can pull your attention away from the game making you hope to do. That gets easier with repetition:

  • Unfamiliar steps become a routine.
  • Less time figuring out where things are.
  • Keeps more of your attention on creating.

A little setup friction now can mean a lot less headache later.

Getting into a creative space with new tools looks different for everyone. Today we're focusing on one piece: getting into Godot and making the basic setup and navigation feel less demanding. You don't need to master the engine today - just get through these first few repetitions so the environment starts to feel more familiar, leaving more of your attention for creating.

Create

Set up your environment

20 min

Your Setup Bundle is your starting point for building - it bundles Godot (the game engine), Backstitch, and the StoryQuest Kit (a set of Threadbare scenes and files). The guide below walks you through setting it up.

For today: complete all of Part 1: Start here in the setup guide. That takes you through Step 6. Stop before Part 2, which covers team and project collaboration you don't need yet.

The StoryQuest Bundle gives you a slightly different starting routine than opening Godot by itself. You'll return to the bundle on your computer and use its launcher file, so Godot opens with the StoryQuest Kit and Backstitch ready to work together.

📖 Guide: Set up your StoryQuest kit ▾

Create

The StoryQuest Bundle

Always remember where the launcher is: using it opens the StoryQuest Kit in Godot with Backstitch ready to work alongside it.

Choose a clear place on your computer to keep the StoryQuest Bundle, somewhere you can find again easily - this folder is your starting point whenever you return to the project. Get familiar with where the launcher is inside that folder. Knowing how to get back here makes starting future sessions much easier.

Let's make a scene!

25 min

Now that your setup is working, it's time to try building something in Godot.

1

Start with the Quick Tour

Take the Quick Tour of Godot to learn the basics you need to know. Looking through it is recommended for everyone, even if you already know the engine - it's a quick orientation that shows what to keep top of mind, and you'll keep learning Godot in the sessions ahead.

2

Build a small playable scene

Use the Setting up a new scene from scratch guide to build your first scene. Scenes are one of the main ways you build and organize things in Godot, so this is a simple first step toward building your StoryQuest.

📖 Guide: Setting up a new scene from scratch ▾

Live guide - if it doesn't load here, open it in a new tab. It updates automatically when the guide changes.

Open: Setting up a new scene from scratch ↗

Starting with a new scene doesn't mean rebuilding everything. You can reuse players, tilemaps, artwork, gameplay elements, and other pieces from the StoryQuest Kit to get a playable area working quickly - a common pattern when building StoryQuests.

Share

Share your scene!

5 min

Take a few minutes to show what you made and where you ended up. Some sharing options:

  • Run your scene and show it in action (project it, show your screen to someone nearby, etc.).
  • Share a screenshot of what you built.

Your task

  • 1Post in the Feed: share a screenshot of your scene, or a quick note about what you tried, changed, or figured out.

This is your first scene, so the goal isn't something polished or complete. Share where you ended up - including anything you tried, changed, or figured out along the way.

It's absolutely ok if you didn't get a chance to "finish" a scene, or if you still have questions or something isn't working yet! You'll keep learning about scenes and building within Godot.
